source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the most common cause of appendicitis?
questions.rationale: The appendix is kinked or occluded by a fecalith, tumor, or foreign body.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Appendicitis (PDF p. 347)
questions.quote: Kinked or occluded by a fecalith

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Pressing the LLQ causes pain in the RLQ. This is:
questions.rationale: Rovsing's sign suggests appendicitis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Appendicitis (PDF p. 347)
questions.quote: Rovsing's sign may be elicited by palpating the left lower quadrant

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Pain that intensifies when pressure over the abdomen is released is called:
questions.rationale: Rebound tenderness indicates peritoneal irritation, as in appendicitis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Appendicitis (PDF p. 347)
questions.quote: Rebound tenderness (ie, production or intensification of pain when pressure is released)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with suspected appendicitis asks for a heating pad and laxative. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: Heat and laxatives can promote perforation; prepare for appendectomy as soon as possible.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Appendicitis (PDF p. 347)
questions.quote: Appendectomy (ie, surgical removal of the appendix) is performed as soon as possible to decrease risk of perforation

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Why is a pregnancy test done for a woman with RLQ pain?
questions.rationale: Ectopic pregnancy can mimic appendicitis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Appendicitis Diagnostics (PDF p. 347)
questions.quote: Pregnancy test- to rule out ectopic pregnancy

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After appendectomy, the client is placed in high-Fowler's position to:
questions.rationale: High-Fowler's reduces incisional and abdominal tension, easing pain.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Appendicitis Nursing (PDF p. 347)
questions.quote: Reduces the tension on the incision and abdominal organs, helping to reduce pain.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which teaching helps a client with hemorrhoids?
questions.rationale: High-residue diet, fluids, sitz baths, and avoiding straining.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hemorrhoids (PDF p. 348)
questions.quote: High-residue diet that contains fruit and bran

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Bright red blood on toilet paper with anal itching most likely indicates:
questions.rationale: Hemorrhoids cause itching, pain, and bright red bleeding.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hemorrhoids (PDF p. 348)
questions.quote: Bright red bleeding

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: The liver prevents ammonia toxicity by converting ammonia to:
questions.rationale: The liver converts ammonia to urea for renal excretion.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hepatobiliary System (PDF p. 348)
questions.quote: Converting ammonia produced from gluconeogenetic by-products and bacteria to urea

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Hepatitis A is transmitted mainly by:
questions.rationale: Hepatitis A and E: fecal-oral; B, C, D: blood and body fluids.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Viral Hepatitis (PDF p. 349)
questions.quote: Hepatitis A Fecal-oral route

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which hepatitis is very severe in pregnant women?
questions.rationale: Hepatitis E resembles A but is very severe in pregnancy.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Viral Hepatitis (PDF p. 349)
questions.quote: Similar to HAV except very severe in pregnant women

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which hepatitis most often leads to chronic liver disease and a carrier state after transfusion?
questions.rationale: Hepatitis C frequently becomes chronic, with cirrhosis and liver cancer risk.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Viral Hepatitis (PDF p. 349)
questions.quote: Frequent occurrence of chronic hepatic cancer carrier state and chronic liver disease.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Jaundice, dark urine, and clay-colored stools appear in which hepatitis stage?
questions.rationale: Icteric stage brings jaundice; pre-icteric is flu-like; post-icteric is convalescence.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hepatitis Stages (PDF p. 349)
questions.quote: Icteric Stage

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Cirrhosis caused by chronic alcoholism and malnutrition is called:
questions.rationale: Laennec's: alcohol; biliary: bile duct disorders; post-hepatic: hepatitis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Liver Cirrhosis (PDF p. 349)
questions.quote: Commonly caused by alcoholism

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Dilated abdominal veins radiating from the umbilicus in cirrhosis are called:
questions.rationale: Caput medusae reflects portal hypertension.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Portal Hypertension (PDF p. 350)
questions.quote: Dilated abdominal vessels radiating from umbilicus (caput medusa)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which daily assessment monitors ascites in portal hypertension?
questions.rationale: Measure and record abdominal girth and weight daily.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Portal Hypertension (PDF p. 350)
questions.quote: Measure & record abdominal girth & body weight daily

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Esophageal varices are caused by:
questions.rationale: Portal hypertension dilates submucosal veins of the lower esophagus.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Esophageal Varices (PDF p. 350)
questions.quote: Caused by portal hypertension

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which item must be at the bedside of a client with a Sengstaken-Blakemore tube?
questions.rationale: Scissors cut the tube to deflate balloons if respiratory distress occurs.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Esophageal Varices (PDF p. 351)
questions.quote: Instrument at the bedside- Scissors

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Hand flapping when the arms are extended with wrists dorsiflexed in liver failure is called:
questions.rationale: Asterixis (liver flap) signals hepatic encephalopathy.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hepatic Encephalopathy (PDF p. 352)
questions.quote: Flapping tremors/Liver flap (Asterixis)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Lactulose is given in hepatic encephalopathy to:
questions.rationale: Lactulose acidifies the colon, traps ammonia, and promotes its evacuation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hepatic Encephalopathy (PDF p. 352)
questions.quote: Administer prescribed medications which may include laxatives (Lactulose)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Why is neomycin given in hepatic encephalopathy?
questions.rationale: Neomycin reduces colonic ammonia-forming bacteria.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hepatic Encephalopathy (PDF p. 352)
questions.quote: Reduce levels of ammonia-forming bacteria in the colon

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Sweet, slightly fecal breath odor in liver failure is:
questions.rationale: Fetor hepaticus is a sign of hepatic encephalopathy.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hepatic Encephalopathy (PDF p. 352)
questions.quote: A sweet, slightly fecal odor to the breath

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Sedatives for a client with cirrhosis should be given in conservative doses because:
questions.rationale: Impaired hepatic metabolism prolongs drug effects.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hepatic Encephalopathy (PDF p. 352)
questions.quote: because liver damage alters drug metabolism

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which is a risk factor for gallstones?
questions.rationale: Risks: obesity, female sex, multiple pregnancies, rapid weight loss, estrogen, diabetes.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Gallbladder Disorders (PDF p. 352)
questions.quote: Rapid weight loss
